topic: Unindexed Updates Trigger Fatal Gap Lock Deadlocks
postText:
During peak admission hours at the hospital where I work, database transactions suddenly seized. No CPU spikes, no memory exhaustion—just deadlocks cascading through emergency queues.

Two concurrent services touched bed state. Service A assigned emergency arrivals; Service B finalized discharge billing. Both queries targeted the same table milliseconds apart.

The root cause was not transaction volume. It was an unindexed filter.

Under default Repeatable Read isolation in MySQL/InnoDB, unindexed row updates force the storage engine to scan the entire clustered index. The database places Next-Key and Gap locks across wide row ranges to prevent phantom reads. Service A held a gap lock on bed records. Service B held an overlapping gap lock from the opposite direction. Neither could acquire an exclusive write lock. Deadlock 1213 fired, aborting admission transactions.

We stabilized the platform with three architectural fixes:
1. Covered Index Scans: Indexed (ward_id, bed_status) so updates grab exact row locks, never gaps.
2. Deterministic Locking: Enforced ascending ID sort on batch operations before calling SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, breaking circular waits.
3. Isolation Tuning: Moved high-write OLTP tables to Read Committed isolation, eliminating phantom-protection gap locks entirely.

Hardware upgrades cannot cure lock contention.

How does your team trace and prevent lock escalation before it exhausts connection pools in high-throughput tables?
